_readme: Built by slice/build_slice.py from timeline.json and data/. Nothing here is authored in this file. Law 01: t is derived from beats[] and everything else is a lookup on t.

5.title: The line that held
5.onScreen: This one did not go out.

6.title: The crossing to Sahul
6.onScreen: They could not see it. They went anyway.

7.title: The others
7.onScreen: If your ancestors left Africa, two percent of you is them.

events.label: The successful dispersal
events.dateNote: REVISED. Formerly written as 60–50 ka broadly; the 2024 admixture genomes tighten the successful exit to shortly before the single Neanderthal gene-flow event at ~50.5–43.5 ka, so the crossing sits nearer 50 ka than 60 ka.
events.why: The emotional core of the film. Everyone alive outside Africa is downstream of this.

events.label: Southern route or Sinai
events.why: MUST render as a diffuse plume, never a line. Where the science has a band, the film draws a band.

events.label: Neanderthal gene flow
events.dateNote: MAJOR REVISION. A single extended gene-flow period centred ~47 ka lasting ~7,000 years, shared by all non-Africans. Formerly written in the storyboard as ~50–60 ka. 1.5–2% Neanderthal ancestry in present-day non-Africans.
events.why: Moved from beat 07 to beat 05. The genetics now says leaving Africa and meeting the others were one continuous event, not two.

events.label: Arrival in Sahul
events.dateNote: Genetic-constrained window: must postdate the shared Neanderthal admixture. Most Sahul archaeological sites fall 54–43 ka.
events.why: RESOLVED — the film does not adjudicate. The ember arrives as a range spanning 65 to 43 ka and the beat says out loud that the rocks and the genomes disagree. This is what the dashed grammar was built for in beat 03, and it is more interesting than either number.

dispute.objection: Madjedbebe's 65 ka is irreconcilable with a post-47 ka admixture in populations that all carry Neanderthal ancestry.
dispute.status: Geneticists and archaeologists openly disagree. Neither line is definitive.

events.label: Madjedbebe
events.dateNote: OSL on 28,500 individual quartz grains from 56 samples.
events.why: Show both dates with equal weight. Neither is the film's answer; the disagreement is.

dispute.objection: Allen and O'Connell argue the sand body is disturbed and younger artefacts have moved downward. They place Sahul colonisation at 47–50 ka. The 2024 admixture genomes independently push the same way.
dispute.status: Contested from two directions at once, and now defended from a third: the 67.8 ka Liang Metanduno stencils put someone in Wallacea before 65 ka.

events.label: Wallacea never bridged
events.dateNote: Minimum open-water crossing of roughly 70–100 km at any Pleistocene sea level. Sunda and Sahul were each continuous land; the gap between them never closed.
events.why: The whole point of the beat. Deliberate watercraft, toward land that could not be seen.

events.label: Liang Metanduno hand stencils
events.dateNote: NEW — published January 2026. Laser-ablation U-series on overlying calcite gives 71.6 ± 3.8 ka, a minimum age of 67.8 ka for the stencil beneath. The oldest securely dated rock art anywhere. Red pigment blown over a hand, with the fingertips deliberately reshaped to points, like claws.
events.why:
CHANGES BEAT 06. The oldest securely dated rock art on earth is in Wallacea, on the road to Sahul, at 67,800 years. The authors read it as strengthening the NORTHERN route through Sulawesi and the Spice Islands into New Guinea - not as a puzzle, as a corridor.

ON-SCREEN FRAMING: 'We cannot identify the hand directly. The authors believe it was ours. If they are right, the northern sea route was being travelled far earlier than the map once allowed.' That keeps the charge without misrepresenting the paper.

authorship.note: CORRECTED. The earlier framing led with 'we do not know whose hand it was', which inverted the paper's own emphasis. The authors acknowledge the maker cannot be identified directly, but they attribute it to Homo sapiens and present it as the oldest direct evidence for modern humans on the northern corridor into Sahul. Denisovans in the region remain a caveat, not the headline.

events.label: Leang Karampuang narrative scene
events.dateNote: ≥51.2 ka. Laser-ablation U-series. Oldest known narrative/representational art.
events.why: NEW, and better than what the storyboard had. Humans, a pig, a scene — storytelling itself, on the migration route, older than the art in Europe. Strongest ground-cut candidate in Act II.

events.label: Leang Tedongnge warty pig
events.dateNote: ≥45.5 ka. Previously the oldest known figurative art.
events.why: The Maros-Pangkep hand stencils (Leang Timpuseng, ≥39.9 ka) supply the match cut: Wallacean islands strung across water hold their arrangement and become splayed fingers. Under the amended Law 04 the stencil's own age no longer has to match the beat, so the shape can be chosen for the cut rather than the calendar. Within the ground shot the camera then finds the Karampuang scene beside it.

events.label: Denisovan gene flow
events.dateNote: Up to ~5% Denisovan ancestry in Papuans. At least two deeply divergent Denisovan lineages contributed.
events.why: Moved here from beat 07 — it is geographically an Island Southeast Asia event, not a European one.

events.label: Neanderthals disappear
events.why: Act II now closes on this rather than on the meeting — the admixture moved to beat 05, the loss stayed here. Structure preserved, chronology fixed.

events.label: Denisova 11 — "Denny"
events.dateNote: First-generation offspring of a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father. Note: predates this beat by ~50,000 years.
events.why: RESOLVED — Denny stays in beat 07. Law 04 was amended: the ground layer is present tense, the evidence as we hold it now, and only the orbital layer rides the time axis. A 90,000-year-old fragment can therefore be exhibited at any beat without breaking Law 01. The clearest case of Law 04 in the film: a first-generation child of two different kinds of human, surviving as one bone.

events.label: Campanian Ignimbrite
events.dateNote: Largest European eruption of the last 200,000 years.
events.why:
DEMOTED. Previously labelled causal for the Neanderthal disappearance and staged as greying the sky 'exactly as their light fails'. Recent work finds no lasting consequence for either Neanderthals or early modern humans, so the causal claim fails - and under Law 06 an event that changes nothing should be cut.

IT SURVIVES ON A DIFFERENT FOOTING: at 39.85 +/- 0.14 ka it is the best-dated tephra horizon in European prehistory. It is HOW WE KNOW the timing of this beat. Under the amended Law 04 the film already has a register for how we know things, and the CI belongs in it. FLAG: this is a genuine Law 06 stress test - the law says causal for what happened, and this is causal for what we can see. Decide whether Law 06 admits epistemic causation or whether the CI gets cut.

routes.label: The line that held, by Bab-el-Mandeb
routes.note: Indicative cartographic path, not a sourced trajectory. The SOUTHERN of the two candidate doors, and for most of this project the only one with geometry - which would have made the renderer choose a route the evidence leaves open. Drawn as a plume alongside breakout-north, at equal weight, neither favoured. See event dispersal-route, confidence 'band'.

routes.label: The line that held, by Sinai
routes.note: Indicative cartographic path, not a sourced trajectory. The NORTHERN of the two candidate doors. It exists because dispersal-route is confidence 'band' and the film had geometry for only one of the two routes it says are unresolved - which meant the renderer would have chosen. Drawn as a plume alongside breakout, at equal weight, neither favoured.
routes.convergence: Both spines end at 57E 23N, where to-sahul begins. That convergence is structural, not evidential: whichever door was used, the line that held went east afterwards, and beat 06 has to be able to pick it up.

routes.label: East to Sahul
routes.note: Indicative cartographic path, not a sourced trajectory. Routes exist so the film can show movement; where the evidence supports a band rather than a line (see event dispersal-route) the renderer must draw a plume along this spine, never the spine itself.

routes.label: Into Europe
routes.note: Indicative cartographic path, not a sourced trajectory. Routes exist so the film can show movement; where the evidence supports a band rather than a line (see event dispersal-route) the renderer must draw a plume along this spine, never the spine itself.

ranges.label: The others
ranges.note: INDICATIVE CARTOGRAPHY, NOT A SOURCED RANGE MAP. A ring drawn to enclose the regions with well-known Neanderthal occupation inside this beat's frame. It is not a distribution, not an isopleth, and not derived from a site database. Confidence is 'band', so the renderer MUST draw it as a diffuse field and never as a boundary line - a hard outline here would claim a frontier that no source supports.
ranges.truncation: Clipped at 60E to the beat's frame. Neanderthals reached the Altai, some 25 degrees further east; the beat's own ground register is a fossil from there. The clip is framing, not evidence.
ranges.retreatNote: Higham 2014 finds the disappearance was spatially staggered rather than simultaneous. The renderer must therefore withdraw this field UNEVENLY and must NOT contract it toward a single last refuge - there is no sourced last refuge, and drawing one would invent the most memorable fact in the beat. The order in which patches go out is fixed noise, carries no dates, and is labelled as such on screen.

sumer2024.cite: Sümer, A. P. et al. (2024). Earliest modern human genomes constrain timing of Neanderthal admixture. Nature 638.
sumer2024.note: The single most consequential source in this file. It moved the dispersal date, moved the admixture into beat 05, and put Madjedbebe under pressure.

iasi2024.cite: Iasi, L. N. M. et al. (2024). Neanderthal ancestry through time. Science.
iasi2024.note: Companion to sumer2024. Single extended gene flow ~47 ka lasting ~7,000 years.

allen-oconnell2020.cite: Allen, J. & O'Connell, J. F. (2020). A different paradigm for the initial colonisation of Sahul. Archaeology in Oceania 55, 1–14.

clarkson2017.cite: Clarkson, C. et al. (2017). Human occupation of northern Australia by 65,000 years ago. Nature 547, 306–310.

bird2018.cite: Bird, M. I. et al. (2018). Palaeogeography and voyage modeling indicates early human colonization of Australia was likely from Timor-Roti. Quaternary Science Reviews 191, 431–439.
bird2018.note: Book or monograph: the citation is correct, but the content has not been re-checked against the physical text.

sulawesi2026.cite: Oktaviana, A. A., Joannes-Boyau, R., Hakim, B. et al. (2026). Rock art from at least 67,800 years ago in Sulawesi. Nature 650, 652-656.
sulawesi2026.note: Published 21 January 2026. Volume and pages verified. Laser-ablation U-series, 71.6 +/- 3.8 ka on overlying calcite, minimum age 67.8 ka for the stencil beneath.

oktaviana2024.cite: Oktaviana, A. A. et al. (2024). Narrative cave art in Indonesia by 51,200 years ago. Nature 631.

brumm2021.cite: Brumm, A. et al. (2021). Oldest cave art found in Sulawesi. Science Advances 7.

aubert2014.cite: Aubert, M. et al. (2014). Pleistocene cave art from Sulawesi, Indonesia. Nature 514, 223–227.
aubert2014.note: Leang Timpuseng hand stencil, minimum age 39.9 ka. Maros-Pangkep stencils range 39.9–17.4 ka.

jacobs2019.cite: Jacobs, G. S. et al. (2019). Multiple deeply divergent Denisovan ancestries in Papuans. Cell 177, 1010–1021.

higham2014.cite: Higham, T., Douka, K., Wood, R. et al. (2014). The timing and spatiotemporal patterning of Neanderthal disappearance. Nature 512, 306–309.

slon2018.cite: Slon, V. et al. (2018). The genome of the offspring of a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father. Nature 561, 113–116.

giaccio2017.cite: Giaccio, B. et al. (2017). High-precision 14C and 40Ar/39Ar dating of the Campanian Ignimbrite (Y-5) reconciles the time-scales of climatic-cultural processes at 40 ka. Scientific Reports 7, 45940.
giaccio2017.note: 40Ar/39Ar: 39.85 ± 0.14 ka at 95% confidence. The film's figure is exact.

wallacea.what: Minimum-bottleneck water crossing from the Sunda shelf to Sahul.
wallacea.definition: Over all island-hopping routes, the smallest achievable longest single hop. Any crossing by any route must include a gap at least this wide.
wallacea.distances: Exact great-circle on unit-sphere coordinates. No projection.
wallacea.notMeasured: This is NOT the Sunda-to-Sahul coastline distance, which is ~994 km at -74 m and is a different quantity.

doors.what: Minimum-bottleneck water crossing out of Africa, measured separately at each of the two candidate doors.
doors.definition: Over all island-hopping routes from the African landmass to the Eurasian landmass THROUGH THIS CORRIDOR ONLY, the smallest achievable longest single water hop. Identical to the Wallacea definition, so the two numbers may be quoted in one sentence.
doors.whyCorridors: Africa and Eurasia share one land component at every sea level in the record, by way of Sinai. A global bottleneck is therefore 0 km and measures nothing. Each corridor isolates one door.
doors.notMeasured: Not the coast-to-coast width of the strait, and not a claim that either door was the one used. timeline.json/dispersal-route is confidence 'band': the route is unresolved and the film does not choose.
doors.grid: ETOPO 2022 bedrock, 60 arc-seconds. Exact great-circle distances on unit-sphere coordinates, no projection.

gulf.what: Share of the Persian Gulf basin standing above the waterline.
gulf.definition: Area fraction of the box above sea level S on ETOPO 2022 bedrock at 60 arc-seconds. Box-relative: quote it only next to this box.

pale.what: The pale light's field: where beat 07 draws the second population.
pale.goesOutAt: Rank in [0,1]. The renderer withdraws a patch when its threshold function of t passes this value. It is a fixed ORDER, not a date, and no patch carries a date.
pale.derivedFrom: timeline.json/ranges/neanderthal-extent, sampled on a 1.9-degree grid and masked to land above -82 m on ETOPO 2022 bedrock.
pale.honesty: INDICATIVE. See the polygon's own note in timeline.json. This is not a distribution and not a site database; it is a field drawn to be diffuse, and the on-screen label says so.
